textbookText: 16. The focal lengths of the two lenses are 20 cm and-20 cm respectively. Mention the types of these two lenses. Out of these two lenses, which one forms a virtual and magnified image when an object is kept 16 cm away from the lens? Explain it by drawing a scaled ray diagram. Ans:- The lens with a focal length of +20 cm is a convex lens, while the lens with a focal length of –20 cm is a concave lens. When an object is placed 16 cm from the lens, it lies between the focal point (20 cm) and the optical center of the convex lens. In this position, a convex lens always forms a virtual, erect, and magnified image on the same side of the lens as the object. This happens because the rays emerging from the lens diverge, and when they are extended backward, they appear to meet at a point behind the object. On the other hand, a concave lens always forms a virtual and diminished image, regardless of object position, so it cannot form a magnified image. Therefore, the convex lens is the one that produces a virtual and magnified image when the object is kept 16 cm away. 17. Identify the type of defect of vision indicated by the given ray diagram. 18 A student in the class has difficulties in seeing the letters written on the whiteboard when he sits on the last bench but he sees them clearly when he sits on the first bench. Based on this, answer the following questions: i) What type of defect of vision does the student have?

Ans:- The student has myopia (short-sightedness) because he cannot see distant objects (letters on the whiteboard from the last bench) clearly but can see nearby objects clearly. ii) Draw a ray diagram showing this type of defect of vision of the student. Excessive curvature of the eye lens – the eye lens becomes too thick and increase its converging power. iv) Explain, with a ray diagram, the role of the lens used to correct this defect. Ans:- Myopia is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens. The concave lens diverges the parallel rays coming from a distant object so that they appear to come from the far point of the myopic eye. After refraction by the eye lens, these rays are focused exactly on the retina, enabling clear distant vision.

19. Explain the laser surgery method used to solve eyesight problems. Ans:- Laser surgery is a modern technique used to correct eyesight problems such as myopia, hypermetropia, and astigmatism. In this method, a highly focused laser beam is used to carefully reshape the cornea, which is the transparent front part of the eye. By adjusting the curvature of the cornea, light rays entering the eye are made to focus correctly on the retina. As a result, vision becomes clear and the dependence on spectacles or contact lenses is reduced or eliminated. 20. What is a cataract? Write the role of the intraocular lens developed by Nepal's ophthalmologist Dr. Sandia Ruit for the treatment of cataracts. Ans:- A cataract is an eye defect in which the natural lens of the eye becomes cloudy or opaque, causing blurred or diminished vision. It usually develops due to ageing but may also occur because of injury, disease, or congenital reasons. Role of intraocular lens developed by Dr. Sanduk Ruit: Nepal’s ophthalmologist Dr. Sanduk Ruit developed a low-cost, high-quality intraocular lens (IOL) used in cataract surgery. During surgery, the cloudy natural lens is removed and replaced with this artificial intraocular lens. The IOL restores clear vision by properly focusing light on the retina, making cataract treatment affordable and accessible, especially in developing countries.
